requirements.requirement: Repair the bundle symlinks so they remain symbolic links, use relative destinations, and point to the intended targets recorded in links.tsv.
requirements.summary: The manifest identifies current → releases/two and latest-report → releases/two/report.txt. Both links were replaced accordingly, and final and post-restart observations confirm those exact relative link values and functional target contents.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the bundle works in its current location and after being copied to another directory.
requirements.summary: Both links resolved to the intended report in place. Two bounded copy tests—before and after restart—directly confirmed that the copied links remained relative and resolved correctly.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the bundle's regular files while repairing the links.
requirements.summary: The two bundle regular files retained their baseline SHA-256 hashes, modes, ownership, sizes, and contents after repair and after restart. The repair command only replaced the two validated symlinks.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were identical before and after execution. The implementation used standard platform utilities and package health remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. The symlinks are relative, remain links, match the manifest, work both in place and after relocation, and persist across a fully evidenced node restart. Regular files, AlmaLinux release, and kernel were preserved.
limitations: Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The symlink replacements were the required repair (cmd-fa41ecefe8eb4d7f). Temporary relocation copies were necessary bounded verification and were removed (cmd-afe63c4f0cb04f2d, cmd-eb0cae6188e24575). The scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-767cbc00f3c443f8). The failed preliminary manifest check was read-only and shows no mutation (cmd-eded338203ab425a). Final snapshots show no failed services, unexpected listeners, package damage, or abandoned test directories. Restart evidence is complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered system, SSH, files, links, and relocation behavior; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree.
